clean-lead-120bpm.gateNote: Label octaves are first-pass estimates, so the required gate is on pitch class. Exact accuracy is still reported; a large exact/pitch-class gap points at the labels, a low pitch-class number points at the detector.

sixteenths.note: 125ms apart at 120bpm. Excluded from the required gate but always reported. Excluding it here is the ONLY sanctioned way to relax this fixture; the labels are never edited.

power-chords-c-a-g-e-c-d-fsharp-e-120bpm.gateNote: This fixture exists to prove power-chord identification, so the gate is on the full label (root + quality "5"). Switch to "pitchClass" to relax it to root-only.

cowboy-chords-c-d-em-g-c-d-em-am-120bpm.gateNote: Major vs minor is the whole point here (C vs Em vs Am), and that lives in the quality, not the root.

chords-a-bm-g-d-2x-120bpm.gateNote: The cleanest strummed-chord case in the set: four open chords, twice through, TWO strums each -- a ringing downstrum then a muted upstrum -- so sixteen events, each one individually recognisable. Major vs minor is the point (A vs Bm), so the gate is on the full label. This fixture was added specifically because strummed chords were not being recognised at all; it is the target the chord path has to hit. Re-articulation matters here as much as identity: a detector that merges each chord's two strums into one event is wrong even if it names the chord correctly, and that shows up as missed events rather than bad labels.

spicy-chords-cmaj9-g-am11.gateNote: Extended voicings. Accuracy is not the criterion — honest abstention is. The real gate is maxFalseLabels: the detector may say "unknown", it may not confidently say the wrong thing.

cowboy-chords-di-d-em-g-c-2x-140bpm.gateNote: HELD-OUT DATA. Added after the 58 engine constants were fitted to the five 120bpm takes; nothing here may be used to retune them. Informational only. Direct-input capture of a 140bpm Les Paul take, D Em G C twice, one bar each. The cleanest of the three captures of this performance -- if the chord path generalises to 140bpm at all, it should show here first.

cowboy-chords-amped-d-em-g-c-2x-140bpm.gateNote: HELD-OUT DATA, informational only. Same performance as the DI take through a Marshall Plexi sim. The amp sim's compression removes almost all envelope contrast between bars, so this is the onset-detection stress case of the set: expect missed re-articulations rather than bad chord names.

cowboy-chords-mic-d-em-g-c-2x-140bpm.gateNote: HELD-OUT DATA, informational only. Room-mic capture of the same performance: real room tone, acoustic path, and a different start offset. Comparing this against the DI take isolates what the microphone path costs the detector, since the notes and their spacing are identical.

power-chords-b-a-g-fsharp-b-a-g-e-140bpm.gateNote: HELD-OUT DATA, informational only. Sixteen root+fifth+octave shapes on the low strings, mic'd through an amp, 857ms apart. Gated on the full label as the 120bpm power-chord fixture is, so a detector that names the root but drops the "5" scores zero here too. Note the pairs: each pitch is played twice, and the second of each pair is muted early, so merging a pair into one event shows up as a missed event.

lead-line-quarter-eighth-triplet-140bpm.gateNote: HELD-OUT DATA, informational only. The 140bpm counterpart to clean-lead-120bpm, but mic'd through an amp instead of clean. Octaves in the labels are measured from the spectrum rather than estimated, so the exact number is meaningful here; the gate still sits on pitch class to stay comparable with the 120bpm fixture.

lead-line-sixteenths-e-fsharp-140bpm.gateNote: HELD-OUT DATA, informational only, and the hardest thing in the corpus: 48 sixteenths 107ms apart, the only test of the 140bpm sixteenth-note requirement anywhere in the fixtures. Four repeats of a pitch per beat, alternating loud downstrokes and quiet upstrokes, so the failure mode to watch for is halving -- 24 events at eighth-note spacing instead of 48. Missed-event count matters more than label accuracy on this one.
